$sources: baseSliceMeters: the slice a work in the round stands on is its scan below 0.04 m, as the stages' sheets measured each cast's base (Data/Stages/classical-hall/Hang.json, the casts' notes: 'the scan's base slice (z < 0.04)').

widthToleranceMeters: the sheets write a scan's width to the millimetre (Hang.json `size`, from the same meshes); five millimetres is past any rounding, so a larger difference means the scan or the plan is not the one the other was measured from.

Media, classical: every work of data/classical.json is a plaster cast of the Royal Cast Collection, SMK (assets/classical/CREDITS.md: 3D scans of plaster casts), shown as the cast: plaster of Paris cast in piece moulds, its seams kept, sized (Data/Matter/Palette.json white.plaster-of-paris, whose roles are the Classical Hall's 41 casts and the Rotunda's four).

Media, Degas: data/sculptures.json's dancer is the wax, with 'bronzes posthumous, from 1922', and asks to label the bronzes as posthumous casts; the Salon shows a bronze (its Hang.json entry, and the collection's scan is the Metropolitan Museum's bronze, assets/sculptures/CREDITS.md), a century indoors under its patina (Palette.json bronze.cusn10 patinated, aged.patina).

Parts, the dancer's skirt: the bronzes wear a real cotton tulle skirt (the Salon's Hang.json support). Its band was measured on the collection's scan at the work's true height of 0.994 m: below 0.33 m the scan is the legs (0.16 m across), from 0.33 m it widens to the skirt (0.26 to 0.35 m across), and at 0.62 m it narrows to the bodice. The scan carries no colour, so the band also takes the hands clasped behind the back at the skirt's top.
